Philippines deploys India’s BrahMos missiles in military exercise amid China-Taiwan tensions

The first confirmed BrahMos field deployment in DAGIT-PA military exercise highlights Manila’s push to defend its northern approaches amid concerns over a potential Taiwan conflict.

Harini Ts

26 November, 2026 07:28 pm IST

New Delhi: The Philippines has fielded its BrahMos shore-based anti-ship missile battery in coordination with naval vessels during its annual joint defence exercise under the looming shadow of a potential China-Taiwan conflict.

The 10th iteration of AFP Joint Exercise (AJEX) DAGITPA 10-2026, held from 17 to 27 November, includes operations in Northern Luzon, Palawan, the National Capital Region, and the Western Command area, focusing on defending the country’s northern maritime approaches in the backdrop of China’s growing naval presence.

The Philippine Marine Corps’ Coastal Defence Regiment (CDR), according to the US Naval Institute (USNI), deployed the missile battery for a joint maritime strike exercise during DAGIT-PA.

Show Full Article

The exercise marks the first confirmed field deployment of the BrahMos system during this series of drills, following earlier rehearsals during Balikatan 2026. It also involved movement of air-defence systems to Northern Luzon, naval escorts protecting military transport and special forces operations on Fuga Island.

WATCH | AFP WRAPS UP AJEX DAGITPA 2026

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) successfully concludes AJEX DAGITPA 10-2026, a ten-day joint and combined exercise held from November 17 to 27 across Northern Luzon and Palawan.

Bringing together the Philippine Army, Philippine… pic.twitter.com/aSNQ7scpiO

— Armed Forces of the Philippines (@TeamAFP) November 26, 2026

The Philippine military said the drills were aimed at strengthening its ability to secure vital maritime approaches, particularly the Luzon Strait.

Also Read: India successfully test-fires JWALA MK-1: Small, cost-effective, smart anti-drone missile from pvt sector

Luzon Strait & its importance Separating the northern Philippines from Taiwan and connecting the South China Sea with the Western Pacific, the Luzon Strait is an important passage for commercial shipping and naval movements.

The strait’s location makes it significant in the event of a conflict over Taiwan. Any escalation could affect the Philippines’ northern islands, including Batanes, and bring the country closer to the military consequences of a cross-strait confrontation. Manila has increased its military presence and conducted area-denial exercises with the US in the region.

Given the presence of commercial shipping routes and undersea communications cables, any military escalation around Taiwan can disrupt maritime traffic and affect regional trade. For the Philippines, the northern islands are particularly exposed to conflict spilling over from Taiwan.

This explains Manila’s increased military activity in northern Luzon and the Batanes region. Deploying BrahMos missiles during DAGIT-PA forms part of its effort to bolster coastal defences and deter hostile naval activity near these strategic approaches.

The Chinese reaction While the BrahMos deployment has not received comparable attention from Chinese state media outlets, several commentators have examined the implications of India’s missile exports to Manila and the potential threat to Chinese naval vessels operating in the South China Sea.

In January 2022, India and the Philippines signed a $375-million contract for three BrahMos anti-ship missile batteries. The agreement made Manila the first foreign customer of the system, jointly developed by India’s Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya. The first delivery took place in April 2024.

Some of the commentators have questioned whether the Philippines has the monitoring, target tracking, communications and operational capabilities required to use the missiles effectively against higher technological opponents.

Their discussions point out that the missile’s performance would depend not only on its speed and range, but also on supporting capabilities such as electronic warfare, reliable communications and a clear operational picture.

India, according to a Reuters report in the first week of November, is in final-stage talks with the Philippines for a potential follow-on deal worth $700 million to $800 million. Manila is considering around five additional systems, involving nearly 60 missiles, and exploring ways to adapt the system to its local environment and logistical framework.

The recent deployment places the BrahMos missile at the centre of Manila’s efforts to strengthen coastal security, while highlighting India’s expanding footprint as an arms supplier in the Indo-Pacific region.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy education minister, officials say

By Nidal al-Mughrabi CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) – Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, medics said, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education in the Gaza Strip, in a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire.

Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and senior officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 Hamas militants in the past month.

Show Full Article

“No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us,” said Netanyahu.

The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw Hamas’ economic portfolio and managed its banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group’s ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had no immediate comment on the allegations about his role.

Two other separate airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday, medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp.

The Israeli military didn’t immediately comment on those seven reported deaths.

Israel has continued to carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by US President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas’ disarmament.

Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.

At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.

Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza’s coast.

Israel’s assault on Gaza has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians since 2023, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced Gaza’s entire population and led to assessments of genocide from scholars and a United Nations inquiry.

Israel has denied the allegations of genocide, saying it acted in self-defense after Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an attack on Israel in October 2023.

(Reporting by Nidal al-Mughrabi; editing by Philippa Fletcher)

BRUSSELS, Nov 26 (Reuters) – EU Council President Antonio Costa on Thursday said his aim for the EU summit was to get member states closer to an agreement on the bloc’s next budget, as several leaders reiterated their objections to proposals he has put on the table.

“My objective is to bring our leaders closer to a deal,” Costa told reporters ahead of the summit in Brussels. “We need a long-term budget fit to funding our main priorities.”

But Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten once again voiced the objections of net contributors to the EU budget, as he said the Netherlands was not ready to accept the proposals on the table.

Show Full Article

“The budget needs to be modernised and needs to be downsized if we want to strike a deal,” Jetten said before the meeting. “It is now up to Costa to come with a better proposal.”

(Reporting by Bart Meijer; Editing by Makini Brice)

Nov 26 (Reuters) – The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo now exceeds 12,000, government data showed on Thursday, as responders continue to struggle to bring the second-largest outbreak on record under control.

• Confirmed infections total 12,021, and 5,904 people have died, the data showed

• The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus, was declared in mid-May in Ituri province in northeastern Congo and has since spread to 8 of Congo’s 26 provinces.

Show Full Article

• There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this species

• Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have led to a more rapid spread than in previous outbreaks

• The current epidemic is the second-largest and deadliest on record behind only the 2014-2016 West African outbreak, which infected more than 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000

• It is not yet under control, as only 15% of new cases come from contacts known to health authorities, according to data presented by Africa CDC earlier this month. That means many chains of transmission continue to be missed

• A Reuters analysis of satellite imagery found the official death toll may be largely underestimated in two of Congo’s hardest-hit areas

(Writing by Clement Bonnerot; Editing by Alexander Winning, Robbie Corey-Boulet and Sonali Paul)
